source.anchor_kjv: I am poured out like water, and all my bones are out of joint... I may tell all my bones: they look and stare upon me.
source.thread: David described the body of a dying man -- bones out of joint from hanging by the arms, every bone countable and exposed, onlookers staring (Ps 22:14,17) -- so exactly it reads like an eyewitness account of a crucifixion, written about 1000 years before Rome made the cross its instrument. This is a DESCRIPTIVE match (the psalm pictures what crucifixion does to a body), not a verbal NT citation. This is what Jesus bore to bring you home; recorded centuries early so you would know none of it was chance -- He was crushed in your place.

source.spoken_script: A king described a dying body so exactly it reads like an eyewitness account of a crucifixion he never saw. Psalm twenty-two. David wrote it in the first person, but he was describing someone else's death, not his own. Watch the body of the dying man: "I am poured out like water, and all my bones are out of joint…" Drained — and every joint pulled loose, the way a body hangs when it's suspended by the arms. And: "I may tell all my bones: they look and stare upon me." He could count every bone, stretched and exposed, while onlookers stood and stared at him. David never saw a crucifixion. Rome would not make it its instrument for centuries. Yet the dying man of his song bears the marks of one — written early. This is what Jesus bore to bring you home — every wrenched joint, every cold stare, recorded centuries early so you'd know none of it was chance. He was crushed in your place.

A king described a dying body so exactly it reads like an eyewitness account of a crucifixion he never saw.

Psalm 22:14 (KJV): "I am poured out like water, and all my bones are out of joint: my heart is like wax; it is melted in the midst of my bowels."

Every joint pulled loose - the way a body hangs when suspended by the arms. Verse 17 adds: the dying man could count every bone, stretched and exposed, while onlookers stared.

David never saw a crucifixion. Rome would not make it its instrument for centuries. Yet his song described it exactly.

This is what Jesus bore to bring you home - every wrenched joint, every cold stare, recorded centuries early so you would know none of it was chance. He was crushed in your place.

platforms.label: YouTube (Long-form 16:9)
platforms.title: Psalm 22 Describes a Crucifixion - Written 1,000 Years Before Rome Made the Cross
platforms.description:
David wrote Psalm 22 in the first person - but he was describing someone else's death, not his own. He was describing a crucifixion he never witnessed, in detail that only makes sense if you know what crucifixion does to a body.

Psalm 22:14 (KJV): "I am poured out like water, and all my bones are out of joint: my heart is like wax; it is melted in the midst of my bowels."

Bones out of joint - that is precisely what happens when a body hangs suspended by the arms, the shoulder joints wrenched from their sockets. Then verse 17: the dying man could count every bone, stretched and visible through the skin, while onlookers stood and stared at him.

This is a descriptive match, not a verbal citation to a specific New Testament verse. But it is a match that should stop you - because Rome would not adopt the cross as an instrument of execution until centuries after David wrote this. And yet the psalm already describes it.

This is what Jesus bore to bring you home. Every wrenched joint. Every cold stare. Recorded centuries early, so you would know: none of it was chance. He was crushed in your place.

Psalm 22 | John 19 | KJV
